title: Sections of the pullback of a quasi-coherent module over an affine open
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $f^*\mathcal G$ its pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$; for an open $W\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(W)$ write $f^*s=\eta_{\mathcal G}(s)\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}W)$. Let $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ be affine opens, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and $\rho:A\to B$, $\rho(a)=f^\sharp_V(a)|_U$, the ring map induced by $f$ (so $B$ is an $A$-algebra and $\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB$ a $B$-module through the second factor). Then the map
$$c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB\longrightarrow(f^*\mathcal G)(U),\qquad s\otimes b\longmapsto b\cdot(f^*s)|_U,$$
is a well-defined isomorphism of $B$-modules, and it is natural in $\mathcal G$: for every $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $(f^*u)_U\circ c_{\mathcal G}=c_{\mathcal G'}\circ(u_V\otimes1_B)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) part (1): psi^* M~ = (S (x)_R M)~ for a morphism of affine schemes Spec S -> Spec R, functorially in M; combined with Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine: G|_V = G(V)~ on an affine V), Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves: global sections of N~ are N) and the compatibility of f^* with restriction to opens (Sheaves, Lemma 00A0, lemma-j-pullback; Modules, Lemma 01AJ, lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback, f^* as a left adjoint); this is the affine description used in the proof of Modules, Lemma 01BG (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent, modules.tex). Stacks states no separate lemma for an affine open U of X lying over an affine open V of Y (statement assembled by the agent).

proof.text: *Step 1 (the affine charts).* Let $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ and $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ be the canonical open immersions with images $V$ and $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Since $U$ and $V$ are affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the isomorphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\cong U$, $\operatorname{Spec}A\cong V$ induce the identity on global sections; so $\iota_U^\sharp$ on sections over $U$ is the identity of $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\iota_V^\sharp$ over $V$ the identity of $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$. Moreover $\iota_V^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and, as $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, $\iota_U^{-1}(f^{-1}V)=\iota_U^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $f(U)\subseteq V$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square] applies to $f$, $U$, $V$, and its ring map ($f^\sharp_V$ followed by restriction to $U$) is $\rho$: with $\psi:=\operatorname{Spec}\rho:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ we have $g:=\iota_V\circ\psi=f\circ\iota_U$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) and Lemma 01I2 (lemma-category-affine-schemes): the reduction to a morphism of affine schemes Spec B -> Spec A, as Stacks does when it applies Lemma 01I9 affine-locally (e.g. Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change, proof, coherent.tex)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\mathcal G$ on $V$ is $\widetilde M$).* Put $M=\mathcal G(V)$, an $A$-module, and let $\mathcal N=\mathcal G|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ be the restriction of $\mathcal G$ along the open immersion $\iota_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]: $\mathcal N(W)=\mathcal G(\iota_V(W))$, so $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal N)=\mathcal G(V)=M$, with $A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)$ acting through $\iota_V^\sharp$, i.e. by the given $A$-module structure (Step 1). By clause (2) of that node $\mathcal N$ is quasi-coherent. Let $\widetilde M$ and $\tau:M\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde M)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3) the counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde M\to\mathcal N$, the morphism corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_M$ under the bijection $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\circ\tau$ of (1), is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules, and $\varepsilon_{\operatorname{Spec}A}(\tau(s))=s$ for $s\in M$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine): a quasi-coherent module on Spec A is the sheaf associated to its global sections; Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) (2)

proof.text: *Step 3 (pullback along the charts is restriction).* By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] for $\iota_V$ there is an isomorphism $\kappa_V:\mathcal N\to\iota_V^*\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules with $\kappa_V(h|_{\iota_V(\iota_V^{-1}W)})=\eta_{\iota_V}(h)$ for $h\in\mathcal G(W)$; for $W=V$ ($\iota_V(\iota_V^{-1}V)=V$, Step 1) this reads $\kappa_V(s)=\eta_{\iota_V}(s)$ for $s\in M=\mathcal N(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. Likewise, with $\mathcal P=(f^*\mathcal G)|_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$ the restriction along $\iota_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], there is an isomorphism $\kappa_U:\mathcal P\to\iota_U^*f^*\mathcal G$ with $\kappa_U(t|_U)=\eta_{\iota_U}(t)$ for $t\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ (take $W=f^{-1}V$; $\iota_U(\iota_U^{-1}W)=U$ by Step 1). Here $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal P)=(f^*\mathcal G)(U)$, and $B=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)$ acts through $\iota_U^\sharp$, i.e. by the given $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$-module structure (Step 1).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00A0 (lemma-j-pullback), last sentence: for an open immersion the pullback of modules is the restriction

proof.text: *Step 4 (composition of pullbacks).* For morphisms of schemes $a:Z\to Z'$, $b:Z'\to Z''$ the functors $(b\circ a)_*$ and $b_*a_*$ are equal (both send $\mathcal H$ to $W\mapsto\mathcal H(a^{-1}b^{-1}W)$ with the same module structure, $(b\circ a)^\sharp=b_*(a^\sharp)\circ b^\sharp$) [def-pc-module-pullback]. Composing the adjunctions $b^*\dashv b_*$ and $a^*\dashv a_*$ gives the composite adjunction $a^*b^*\dashv b_*a_*$ with unit $b_*(\eta_{a,b^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta_{b,\mathcal H}$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to it, to $(b\circ a)^*\dashv(b\circ a)_*$ and to $\delta=\mathrm{id}:(b\circ a)_*\to b_*a_*$ gives an isomorphism $c_{b,a}:a^*b^*\to(b\circ a)^*$ of functors with $(b\circ a)_*(c_{b,a,\mathcal H})\circ b_*(\eta_{a,b^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta_{b,\mathcal H}=\eta_{b\circ a,\mathcal H}$; on sections over an open $W\subseteq Z''$: $c_{b,a}(\eta_a(\eta_b(h)))=\eta_{b\circ a}(h)$ in $\Gamma(a^{-1}b^{-1}W,(b\circ a)^*\mathcal H)$ for $h\in\mathcal H(W)$. Apply this to $(b,a)=(f,\iota_U)$ and to $(b,a)=(\iota_V,\psi)$, whose composites are both $g$ (Step 1), and put $\Lambda=c_{\iota_V,\psi,\mathcal G}^{-1}\circ c_{f,\iota_U,\mathcal G}:\iota_U^*f^*\mathcal G\to\psi^*\iota_V^*\mathcal G$, an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$-modules. For $s\in M=\mathcal G(V)$ (with $g^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$) both $\eta_{\iota_U}(\eta_f(s))$ and $\eta_\psi(\eta_{\iota_V}(s))$ go to $\eta_g(s)$, so $\Lambda(\eta_{\iota_U}(\eta_f(s)))=\eta_\psi(\eta_{\iota_V}(s))$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules): (g o f)_* = g_* o f_* and the canonical isomorphism (g o f)^* = f^* o g^* obtained from it by uniqueness of adjoints

proof.text: *Step 5 (Schemes 01I9 (1) for $\psi$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] applied to $\rho:A\to B$ and $\psi=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$, there is an isomorphism $\theta:\psi^*\widetilde M\to\widetilde{B\otimes_AM}$ of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$-modules with $\theta(\eta_\psi(\tau(s)))=\tau(1\otimes s)$ for $s\in M$. The morphism $\kappa_V\circ\varepsilon:\widetilde M\to\iota_V^*\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism (Steps 2, 3), hence so is $\psi^*(\kappa_V\circ\varepsilon)$ (a functor [def-pc-module-pullback] preserves isomorphisms), and naturality of the unit of $\psi^*\dashv\psi_*$ gives $\psi^*(\kappa_V\varepsilon)(\eta_\psi(\tau(s)))=\eta_\psi(\kappa_V(\varepsilon(\tau(s))))=\eta_\psi(\kappa_V(s))=\eta_\psi(\eta_{\iota_V}(s))$ in $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\psi^*\iota_V^*\mathcal G)$ (Steps 2, 3).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) (1): psi^* M~ = (S (x)_R M)~ functorially in M

proof.text: *Step 6 (the isomorphism on sections).* Let $\Omega=\theta\circ\psi^*(\kappa_V\varepsilon)^{-1}\circ\Lambda\circ\kappa_U:\mathcal P\to\widetilde{B\otimes_AM}$, a composite of isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$-modules (Steps 3, 4, 5). On global sections it gives a bijection $\Omega_{\operatorname{Spec}B}:(f^*\mathcal G)(U)\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\widetilde{B\otimes_AM})$ which is $B$-linear (a morphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$-modules is linear over $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$ on global sections, and by Step 3 this is the given $B$-structure of $(f^*\mathcal G)(U)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2) (over $B$), $\tau:B\otimes_AM\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\widetilde{B\otimes_AM})$ is a $B$-linear bijection; put $\Phi=\tau^{-1}\circ\Omega_{\operatorname{Spec}B}:(f^*\mathcal G)(U)\to B\otimes_AM$, a $B$-linear bijection. For $s\in M$, with $f^*s=\eta_f(s)\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$: $\kappa_U((f^*s)|_U)=\eta_{\iota_U}(\eta_f(s))$ (Step 3), $\Lambda$ sends it to $\eta_\psi(\eta_{\iota_V}(s))$ (Step 4), $\psi^*(\kappa_V\varepsilon)^{-1}$ to $\eta_\psi(\tau(s))$ and $\theta$ to $\tau(1\otimes s)$ (Step 5); hence $\Phi((f^*s)|_U)=1\otimes s$ and, by $B$-linearity, $\Phi(b\cdot(f^*s)|_U)=b\otimes s$. Let $\sigma:\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_A\mathcal G(V)$, $s\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes s$, be the swap isomorphism of $B$-modules. Then $\Phi^{-1}\circ\sigma$ is a $B$-linear isomorphism sending $s\otimes b$ to $b\cdot(f^*s)|_U$; it is therefore the map $c_{\mathcal G}$ of the statement, which is thus well defined and an isomorphism of $B$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) (2): Gamma(Spec R, M~) = M; Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) (1)

proof.text: *Step 7 (naturality).* Let $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be $\mathcal O_Y$-linear between quasi-coherent modules. Both $(f^*u)_U\circ c_{\mathcal G}$ and $c_{\mathcal G'}\circ(u_V\otimes1_B)$ are $B$-linear maps $\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB\to(f^*\mathcal G')(U)$, and $\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB$ is generated as a $B$-module by the $s\otimes1$, so it suffices to compare them there. Naturality of the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $f_*f^*(u)\circ\eta_{f,\mathcal G}=\eta_{f,\mathcal G'}\circ u$, on sections over $V$ gives $(f^*u)_{f^{-1}V}(f^*s)=f^*(u_V(s))$; as $f^*u$ commutes with restriction to $U$, $(f^*u)_U(c_{\mathcal G}(s\otimes1))=(f^*u)_U((f^*s)|_U)=(f^*(u_Vs))|_U=c_{\mathcal G'}(u_V(s)\otimes1)$.
